column1: # h2spec 2.6.0's failures against gaato/mttp_ng's HTTP/2 server that are
# known and explained (scripts/h2spec.mbtx), run with -P /wait so that a
# request's stream is still open when the next frame of a test arrives. A
# failure not listed here fails the script, and so does a listed one that
# passes, so the list only shrinks. Columns, separated by one tab: the mode
# (tls or h2c), h2spec's package, its test case, and why it fails.

column3: closed: Sends a DATA frame after sending RST_STREAM frame
column4: nghttp2 drops frames for a stream it no longer keeps: the server answered and closed the stream before the frame came, and nghttp2 1.71 as configured here does not retain it, so it cannot tell the stream from one never used (lib/nghttp2_session.c, session_on_data_received_fail_fast).

column3: closed: Sends a HEADERS frame after sending RST_STREAM frame
column4: nghttp2 drops frames for a stream it no longer keeps: the server answered and closed the stream before the frame came, and nghttp2 1.71 as configured here does not retain it, so it cannot tell the stream from one never used (lib/nghttp2_session.c, session_on_data_received_fail_fast).

column3: Sends stream identifier that is numerically smaller than previous
column4: nghttp2 ignores a HEADERS frame whose stream it no longer keeps instead of answering PROTOCOL_ERROR (it cannot tell an old identifier from a reused one); the frame is dropped, not processed.

column3: Sends PRIORITY frame that depend on itself
column4: nghttp2 does not validate PRIORITY frames: RFC 9113 deprecated their signal (section 5.3.2), and nghttp2 parses the frame but acts on none of it.

column3: Sends a PRIORITY frame with 0x0 stream identifier
column4: nghttp2 does not validate PRIORITY frames: RFC 9113 deprecated their signal (section 5.3.2), and nghttp2 parses the frame but acts on none of it.

column3: Sends multiple WINDOW_UPDATE frames increasing the flow control window to above 2^31-1 on a stream
column4: nghttp2 ends the whole connection with GOAWAY(FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR) where h2spec expects only the stream reset; RFC 9113, section 6.9.1 lets the endpoint terminate the stream or the connection.

With h2c the cleartext port also serves HTTP/1.1, and bytes that are not the HTTP/2 preface are taken as an HTTP/1.1 request (@h2server.serve): the server waits for its head instead of answering GOAWAY.
